notes: Read SKILL.md and references/details.md in full. The skill explains authentication vs authorization and gives TypeScript/Express samples for JWT access/refresh tokens, Redis-backed sessions, Passport Google OAuth, RBAC, permission checks, resource ownership, bcrypt password hashing and rate limiting, plus best practices and pitfalls.

No commands, installs, credentials, or network access for the agent; secrets appear only as process.env references (JWT_SECRET, SESSION_SECRET, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET) in application code the user writes, with no instruction to read, print or send real values.

Review samples before copying: the OAuth callback passes the access token in a redirect query string (references/details.md:297-299), which leaks into logs/history; refresh tokens are looked up by `await hash(refreshToken)` (references/details.md:90, 111), which only works with a deterministic hash such as SHA-256, not salted bcrypt; and `requireOwnership` is declared async so it returns a Promise rather than middleware (references/details.md:412). These are code-quality caveats, not unsafe agent behavior.
